name: transposed_out_add
targeted_gap: byte model treats block_sizes[n-1] as contiguous, but the store is to a transposed output view whose innermost tiled axis has stride M
hypothesis: seed gives the innermost tiled dim (block 1) a big 1024-elem tile, but on the transposed output out[tm,tn] that axis has stride M, so 1024 consecutive tn stores land M elems apart => zero store coalescing (1024 separate cache lines, 1 row). default [32,32] writes 32 contiguous runs of 32 along the actually-contiguous block-0 (tm) axis, so it coalesces far better and beats the seed.

name: transposed_in_relu2
targeted_gap: innermost tiled axis maps to a transposed INPUT view (stride M); the loads a big inner tile drags are non-contiguous but the byte model (slab==1) is blind to it
hypothesis: traffic-2 relu-squared => seed picks an even bigger inner tile [1,2048]. The input xT is a transposed view so xT[tm,tn] has stride M along tn; 2048 consecutive tn loads are each M elems apart => the load coalesces terribly (2048 distinct 128B lines, one element used each). default [32,32] reads 32 contiguous 32-runs along the contiguous tm axis, so it coalesces and wins by >10%.

name: transposed_both_scale
targeted_gap: BOTH the input read and the output store are transposed views (stride M on the innermost tiled axis); fp32 widens each strided element so the coalescing penalty is per-4-bytes
hypothesis: fp32 scale => bpe=8 gives seed inner tile [1,1024]. Both xT[tm,tn] (load) and out[tm,tn] (store) are transposed, so the innermost axis has stride M on BOTH sides: 1024 consecutive tn indices are M*4 bytes apart => every load AND store is a fresh cache line with one 4B element used. default [32,32] gets contiguous runs along the block-0 tm axis on both, coalescing far better, so the seed is drastically slower.
